# Preface {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/book.R")
```

R's arrays are a vector with a `dim` attribute, and R's `[` is one of the
richest indexing languages there is. ALTREP lets a package supply the
vector: the values can live in a Zarr store on object storage, in NetCDF
files behind a reference table, or in an Icechunk repository, and be read
only when R asks for them. The object has no class. To R, and to every
function ever written for arrays, it is an array.

That works today, with one gap. When you write `x[i, j, k]`, R asks the
object for the result one element at a time. A store that could have fetched
the 60 chunks it needs in one concurrent batch instead sees millions of
single-element questions and answers them chunk by chunk, in series.

The proposed change to R is one optional ALTREP method,
`Extract_array_subset`: about 100 lines that let R hand the whole request
over. This book is the case for it, made with reads from real stores.

The short version:

- `x[cbind(i, j, k)]` and `x[i]` already reach an ALTREP array whole, on
  any released R. Planned point extraction works now (@sec-points).
- `x[i, j, k]` and `m[i, j]` do not. Same chunks, same bytes, but one
  round trip per chunk instead of one batch (@sec-rectangles).
- On real stores that is the difference between a map arriving in one
  merged request and in 60 (@sec-cmems, @sec-virtual, @sec-sharded,
  @sec-icechunk).
- With the method, code that knows nothing about lazy arrays gets planned
  reads: `apply()`, loops, negative and logical and character subscripts
  (@sec-ordinary).
- The patch changes nothing for any existing class, and the package ABI
  does not move (@sec-patch).

## How to read the tables

Every table in this book is produced when the book is rendered. Each
example is a script in
[`book/scripts`](https://github.com/mdsumner/r-variants/tree/main/book/scripts)
that is run twice: once with stock R-devel and once with R-devel plus the
patch, both in the same container, with the same altarr and zaro source.
The columns:

- **Chunks**: distinct chunks the read needs. The same in both builds.
- **Fetch calls**: how many times R's requests reached the store as a
  batch. One is the goal.
- **Requests** and **MB**: HTTP requests sent and bytes received, for
  stores read over the network.
- **Seconds**: wall time. The patched build runs first, so a warm cache
  anywhere along the way counts against the patch, not for it.
- **Same values**: the two builds returned the same numbers.

Timings from a live store are one run on one day; read them as ratios, not
benchmarks. Where a table's caption says "Earlier run", this render did not
reach that store and the last saved result is shown instead.
